interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switches between the flat 2D view of the approximating rectangle R_k and the 3D cylindrical shell S_k it generates, making the correspondence between a thin strip and its revolved shell explicit

interactions.label: Strip k
interactions.teaches: Selecting the kth rectangle in panel (a) simultaneously lights up the matching cylindrical shell S_k in panel (b), making the radius x_k, height f(x_k), and shell volume 2π·x_k·f(x_k)·Δx visually concrete

interactions.label: Number of strips n
interactions.teaches: Increasing n makes every shell thinner (smaller Δx) and the Riemann sum of shell volumes converge to the true volume, illustrating the limit defining the shell-method integral 2π∫x·f(x)dx

demo_steps.title: The 2D rectangle
demo_steps.narration: Panel (a) shows the decreasing curve with a single teal rectangle R_k spanning from x_{k-1} to x_k. This thin vertical strip approximates the kth slice of the region under the curve.

demo_steps.title: Revolve to form a shell
demo_steps.narration: Switch to panel (b): the same rectangle, revolved about the y-axis, produces a hollow cylindrical shell S_k. Its radius is x_k, height is f(x_k), and thickness is Δx. The top rim clearly shows the annular cross-section.

demo_steps.title: Sweep k outward
demo_steps.narration: Drag k from 1 toward n. The shell moves outward with increasing radius while its height decreases following the curve — each shell samples a different (radius, height) pair.

demo_steps.title: Refine the partition
demo_steps.narration: Raise n to 30. The shells become thin nested rings and the Riemann sum Σ 2π·x_k·f(x_k)·Δx approaches the exact integral, demonstrating convergence of the shell method.

plan.geometry_notes: Two-panel layout switched via toggle. Panel (a) is drawn entirely in the XY screen plane (flat, front-on): axes span x ∈ [0, 3.5] and y ∈ [0, 4.2]; curve f(x) = 4 − 0.35x² over [0.5, 3.0], teal #14b8b8, 3px line; rectangle R_k filled #bfe3e0 with #14b8b8 border, width Δx, height f(x_k); caption '(a) Rectangle approximating the kth strip' at y = −0.6. Panel (b) uses 3D geometry: cylinders centered at world origin with vertical Y-axis. Shells are WIDE and FLAT: scale factor 1.4 on radii so outer shell reaches ~4.2 world-units radius; height scale 0.8 so tallest shell is ~3.2 units — giving a wide, squat appearance with clearly visible top rims. Each shell drawn as two open-ended CylinderGeometry surfaces (outer radius x_k·1.4, inner radius x_{k-1}·1.4, height f(x_k)·0.8) in translucent grey #aaaaaa opacity 0.18, plus two RingGeometry annuli (top and bottom) in grey opacity 0.35. The highlighted S_k is a tall vertical band: a partial-arc cylinder sector with thetaLength = 0.9 rad (~50°), full height f(x_k)·0.8, rendered in solid teal #14b8b8 opacity 0.85 with a lighter top rim #7dd4d4. Label 'S_k' placed beside the band. Caption '(b) Cylindrical shell generated by the rectangle' below at y = −0.8. Colors: teal #14b8b8, light fill #bfe3e0, grey shells #aaaaaa, axes #333333. For n strips: Δx = (3.0−0.5)/n, x_k = 0.5 + k·Δx. Exact volume V = 2π∫₀.₅³ x(4−0.35x²)dx ≈ 65.5.
plan.notes: Panel (a) group is a flat 2D scene in the XY plane — no Z displacement — so it always appears front-on regardless of orbit state; orbit controls only affect panel (b) group. On toggle switch, hide one group and show the other with a brief fade. Panel (b) shells: use CylinderGeometry with openEnded=true for side walls, RingGeometry for top/bottom annular caps. The S_k highlight uses CylinderGeometry with thetaStart/thetaLength to create a partial-arc band that reads as a tall vertical stripe. Rebuild all shell geometry reactively when numStrips or stripIndex changes. Render top rims with slightly higher opacity and a subtle edge line so the hollow annular cross-section is unmistakable. HTML overlay shows numeric readout (radius, height, Δx, shell volume, cumulative sum).

authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the shell method for computing volumes of solids of revolution about the y-axis. Panel (a): the 2D xy-plane showing a decreasing curve with a single rectangular strip Rk spanning from x_{k-1} to xk approximating the kth vertical strip of the region; a rotation arrow near the y-axis indicates revolution about that axis. Caption: Rectangle approximating the kth strip. Panel (b): a 3D view of the cylindrical shell Sk generated by revolving the rectangle about the y-axis, shown as a hollow cylindrical ring. Caption: Cylindrical shell generated by the rectangle. The figure introduces the shell method by showing how each thin vertical rectangle, when revolved, produces a cylindrical shell whose volume approximates the corresponding tubular portion of the solid.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for strip index k: select the kth rectangle in panel (a) and simultaneously highlight the corresponding cylindrical shell Sₖ in panel (b), displaying its radius, height, and volume
- Slider for number of strips n: increase n and watch the shells become thinner, with the total shell volume sum converging to the true solid volume
- Drag to rotate the 3D cylindrical shell in panel (b) to inspect its geometry from any angle
authoredContext: As a rule, the tubes will have curved upper surfaces, so there will be no simple formulas for their volumes. However, if the strips are thin, then we can approximate each strip by a rectangle (Figure 5.3.4a). These rectangles, when revolved about the y-axis, will produce cylindrical shells whose volumes closely approximate the volumes of the tubes generated by the original strips (Figure 5.3.4b). We will show that by adding the volumes of the cylindrical shells we can obtain a Riemann sum that approximates the volume V, and by taking the limit of the Riemann sums we can obtain an integral for the exact volume V .
sourceQmd: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.3.4

demo_steps.title: One rectangle → one shell
demo_steps.narration: With n=8 and k=4, the teal rectangle R_k in panel (a) revolves about the y-axis to produce the highlighted teal shell S_k in panel (b). Its radius is x_k, its height is f(x_k), and its volume is ≈ 2π·x_k·f(x_k)·Δx.

demo_steps.title: Sweep k across the region
demo_steps.narration: Drag k from 1 to n. The highlighted shell moves outward and grows in radius while its height follows the curve, showing how each shell samples a different radius and height.

demo_steps.title: Refine the partition
demo_steps.narration: Raise n to 40. The shells become thin rings and the displayed sum Σ 2π·x_k·f(x_k)·Δx approaches the exact volume V = 2π∫x·f(x)dx, demonstrating convergence of the shell method.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World layout: panel (a) occupies the left half (x ∈ [-7,-2], y ∈ [0,4.5]) drawn in the world XY plane; panel (b) cylinder centered near x=+3.5 with vertical y-axis (y ∈ [0,4.5]). Strip domain on the curve: x ∈ [a,b] = [0.5, 3.0]; curve f(x) = 4 - 0.35·x^2 (decreasing, concave-down, positive on the domain). For n strips, Δx=(b-a)/n, x_k = a + k·Δx. Shell k: inner radius x_{k-1}, outer radius x_k, height f(x_k); draw as hollow cylinder (outer CylinderGeometry radius x_k, inner radius x_{k-1}, height f(x_k)) in translucent grey #cccccc opacity ~0.22 with elliptical rim rings; the selected shell rendered as a teal #14b8b8 wedge/sector (≈40° arc) with light-teal #bfe3e0 fill and the teal curve arc on its top rim. Exact volume V = 2π∫_{0.5}^{3} x(4-0.35x^2)dx ≈ 65.46 (compute numerically). Colors: curve/edges teal #14b8b8, highlight fill #bfe3e0, shell body grey #cccccc, axes black. Scale radii by ~1.0 world-unit per x-unit and heights by ~1.0 per y-unit so the cylinder is ~3 units radius and ~3-4 units tall.
interactionPlan.notes: Build panel (b) shell with two open-ended CylinderGeometry surfaces (outer + inner) plus two ring/annulus meshes for top and bottom rims; the highlighted S_k is a partial-angle cylinder sector (thetaLength ≈ 0.7 rad) so the hollow interior stays visible. Recompute all n shells and the selected highlight reactively on both sliders; keep a single group for shells and rebuild on n change. Show the numeric readout (radius, height, shell volume, Σ sum, exact V) as an HTML overlay updated each frame. Orbit controls target the panel (b) cylinder center; panel (a) is a flat reference that may tilt slightly under orbit, which is acceptable for a 3D scene.

demo_steps.narration: Raise n to 30. The shells become thin nested rings and the Riemann sum Σ 2π·x_k·f(x_k)·Δx approaches the exact integral, demonstrating convergence of the shell method.

plan.geometry_notes: Two-panel layout switched via toggle. Panel (a) is drawn entirely in the XY screen plane (flat, front-on): axes span x ∈ [0, 3.5] and y ∈ [0, 4.2]; curve f(x) = 4 − 0.35x² over [0.5, 3.0], teal #14b8b8, 3px line; rectangle R_k filled #bfe3e0 with #14b8b8 border, width Δx, height f(x_k); caption '(a) Rectangle approximating the kth strip' at y = −0.6. Panel (b) uses 3D geometry: cylinders centered at world origin with vertical Y-axis. Shells are WIDE and FLAT: scale factor 1.4 on radii so outer shell reaches ~4.2 world-units radius; height scale 0.8 so tallest shell is ~3.2 units — giving a wide, squat appearance with clearly visible top rims. Each shell drawn as two open-ended CylinderGeometry surfaces (outer radius x_k·1.4, inner radius x_{k-1}·1.4, height f(x_k)·0.8) in translucent grey #aaaaaa opacity 0.18, plus two RingGeometry annuli (top and bottom) in grey opacity 0.35. The highlighted S_k is a tall vertical band: a partial-arc cylinder sector with thetaLength = 0.9 rad (~50°), full height f(x_k)·0.8, rendered in solid teal #14b8b8 opacity 0.85 with a lighter top rim #7dd4d4. Label 'S_k' placed beside the band. Caption '(b) Cylindrical shell generated by the rectangle' below at y = −0.8. Colors: teal #14b8b8, light fill #bfe3e0, grey shells #aaaaaa, axes #333333. For n strips: Δx = (3.0−0.5)/n, x_k = 0.5 + k·Δx. Exact volume V = 2π∫₀.₅³ x(4−0.35x²)dx ≈ 65.5.
plan.notes: Panel (a) group is a flat 2D scene in the XY plane — no Z displacement — so it always appears front-on regardless of orbit state; orbit controls only affect panel (b) group. On toggle switch, hide one group and show the other with a brief fade. Panel (b) shells: use CylinderGeometry with openEnded=true for side walls, RingGeometry for top/bottom annular caps. The S_k highlight uses CylinderGeometry with thetaStart/thetaLength to create a partial-arc band that reads as a tall vertical stripe. Rebuild all shell geometry reactively when numStrips or stripIndex changes. Render top rims with slightly higher opacity and a subtle edge line so the hollow annular cross-section is unmistakable. HTML overlay shows numeric readout (radius, height, Δx, shell volume, cumulative sum).
